title: How good can ai work?
author: SuggestionSevere2461
selftext: Okay. I have zero coding experience. If I am very specific with my writing will Claude be able to make the game I want? Im looking into making something with graphics similar to Última 6/Tibia. Just wondering if it's worth trying the 100$ sub option.

comments.author: ontagi
comments.body: Are you experienced with AI usage. Like, seriously experienced? Nut just a 20 bucks plan you use every now and then. If not, this could be a hard time and take quite a while

comments.author: alanbdee
comments.body: It can do it sure. But remember that you're what separates AI from AI slop. You're the director. You decide if it's good enough. Being picky will be a good thing.

comments.author: StellarSoupStudio
comments.body:
It's an accelerant. You'll be able to do much more if you research how graphics works. Like read the Wikipedia articles on computer graphics. Learn how 3d models work, what a the normal of a plane is, what sub surface scattering is, what a ray is and why you'd want to trace it.

Being precise helps but having developing an understanding of what happens will make feedback way easier to give and keep your token cost down.

comments.author: Middle-Moist
comments.body: Get a really good harness of your are planning on making a large game. I am in the same boat as you so I trained me a tool to catch all the mistakes id never be able to see in time

comments.author: MaqeSweden
comments.body:
You can try the $20 option to get started and get a feel for if it seems to indicate it can do what you want from it.

Get the cheap option and just talk to it and tell it everything you're thinking and that you're a newbie at vibe coding and need all the help you can get.

Do a quick test to begin with - but if you decide to build a serious game, you want to prompt it that that is your ambition and that you want it to be coded as a serious game and set rules that you need to be guided and interpreted in a way that your vibecoding inputs doesn't mess up the structure of the game too much.

But from the reference games you mention - yes, it can easily do that.

comments.author: Own_Badger6076
comments.body: I'd probably start with a 20$ sub and leverage claude  code then go from there.  It can produce good quality work, but if you're looking for "I one shotted this game" youtube influencer experience you're gonna be disappointed.

comments.author: Upper-Gazelle-4967
comments.body: It can suck a golf ball through a cocktail straw

comments.author: NagatoKami
comments.body: Prepare yourself for a lot of tweaking with a clanker.

comments.author: Natural-Comedian6670
comments.body: It helps if you’ve developed games .. just like I’m sure Claude could tell me how to repair an engine but without the knowledge of how engines work it won’t get me all the way . Even just making art is a vast array of disciplines to do it well and that’s without even being original or developing a style . Start small and simple , even copying a derivative game will teach you a lot .. it might not be released, but can help a great deal to get familiar with unity / unreal or whatever you might use .

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
AI can code better than humans.

Whether or not it can make a cohesive game is on you, though, and how much time and effort you devote to to it. If you're looking for an RPG, you're looking at a thousand hours or so if I had to guess. The only games you can really make somewhat fast are small scope or rely heavily on procedural elements.  Actual level/worldbuilding is not exactly AI's strength so you'll be stuck doing a lot of manual work. If you're not trying to publish it and not really looking to invest a lot of time, you're better off  just getting AI to mod and improve your favorite game.

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body:
I say start trying to create a tiny, tiny game. Start planning with ai, ask what engine to use for your project. Start asking questions and do things manually. Then start using Claude or codex and have it handle your code and things in the editor. Try your best to understand the every file and folder within your project folder. Don’t go full vibecode right away.

You can do it! I am! My project is organized and I no longer have fear of it breaking because ai is getting better and I mostly understand what’s going on I just haven’t memorized a bunch of syntax!

comments.author: SuggestionSevere2461
comments.body: Thanks for the replies. I will try the 20$ option

replies.author: Hotwingz66
replies.body:
Some word of advice, read up on how to structure a game. You do need some insight in how systems behind a game work.

As an example, if your game has an inventory, that shouldnt have to live in the player character script for example.

You'll have to guide your AI to seperate systems so it doesn't just make things work. Like having skill logic tied to the specific skill icon to your hotbar as another example.

When you think you have a good idea of separation of responsibilities, you can always ask your agent what it thinks and how they would implement it.

That should help you get started.

Good luck!

comments.author: Tiamitsu
comments.body: I would recommend watching tutorials on game design, as well as on AI. Then, experiment by first creating small prototypes and testing out concepts that interest you and that you find engaging in a game. One piece of advice I would offer is to be very organized in your work.

comments.author: Any-Blacksmith-2054
comments.body: First, for 2D $20 is enough. Then talk in voice with Claude (this is simply faster, in your local language if not native English) and discuss all aspects of your game. Ask to create ~10 prompts for chatgpt to create reference arts (yes free chatgpt will create you 10 highly detailed images for free), then ask to create series of prompts for Claude code and execute them. It will take just several hours. And share what you get with me dude 😎

comments.body:
Why don’t you start with a cheaper sub option ($20) and iterate through it. Here’s a good series on building a game with Claude as a beginner:

comments.author: Significant-Syrup400
comments.body: It's recommended to learn how to code.  Ai can produce significantly better results with proper systems planning and targeted prompting and do it with far less tokens.
